arxiv-2005-12730.title: Electromagnetic field energy in an absorptive medium with temporal and spatial dispersion
arxiv-2005-12730.creator: A.G. Zagorodny ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}, S.A. Trigger ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}, A.I. Momot ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}
arxiv-2005-12730.description: Abstract General relations for electromagnetic field energy outside the transparency domain are proposed. It is shown that charged particle contribution to the energy of electromagnetic perturbations in the general case can be described in terms of a bilinear combination of the dielectric polarizability of the medium. The explicit form of such contribution is found.

arxiv-2012-01352.title: Ellipsograph of Archimedes as a simple LEGO construction
arxiv-2012-01352.creator: Sara Jodlbauer, Zoltán Kovács
arxiv-2012-01352.description: Abstract We report on a simple LEGO construction that can draw an ellipse by using the concept of trammel of Archimedes. School curriculum related to elementary geometry usually focuses on “compass and ruler” constructions where the traditional Euclidean construction steps are allowed to generate a figure.

arxiv-2103-13727.title: Conway’s spiral and a discrete Gömböc with 21 point masses Thanks: Support of the NKFIH Hungarian Research Fund Grant No. 134199 and Grant No. TKP2021 BME-NVA is kindly acknowledged.
arxiv-2103-13727.creator: Gábor Domokos, Flórián Kovács
arxiv-2103-13727.description: Abstract . We show an explicit construction in 3 dimensions for a convex, mono-monostatic polyhedron (i.e., having exactly one stable and one unstable equilibrium) with 21 vertices and 21 faces. This polyhedron is a 0-skeleton, with equal masses located at each vertex.

arxiv-2306-05309.title: SMUG Planner: A Safe Multi-Goal Planner for Mobile Robots in Challenging Environments
arxiv-2306-05309.creator: Changan Chen, Jonas Frey, Philip Arm, Marco Hutter
arxiv-2306-05309.description: Abstract Robotic exploration or monitoring missions require mobile robots to autonomously and safely navigate between multiple target locations in potentially challenging environments. Currently, this type of multi-goal mission often relies on humans designing a set of actions for the robot to follow in the form of a path or waypoints.

arxiv-2405-18130.title: SMART: spectral energy distributions Markov chain analysis with radiative transfer models
arxiv-2405-18130.creator: Charalambia Varnava and Andreas Efstathiou
arxiv-2405-18130.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Charalambia Varnava and Andreas Efstathiou. In this paper we present the publicly available open-source spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting code SMART (Spectral energy distributions Markov chain Analysis with Radiative Transfer models). Implementing a Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method, SMART fits the ultraviolet to millimetre SEDs of galaxies exclusively with radiative transfer models that currently constitute four types of pre-computed libraries, which describe the starburst, active galactic nucleus (AGN) torus, host galaxy and polar dust components.

arxiv-2407-09707.title: Coherent J/ ψ \psi photoproduction and polarization in peripheral Pb–Pb collisions with ALICE
arxiv-2407-09707.creator: L. Massacrier for the ALICE Collaboration
arxiv-2407-09707.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by L. Massacrier for the ALICE Collaboration. Photonuclear reactions are induced by the strong electromagnetic field generated by ultrarelativistic heavy ions. These processes have been extensively studied in ultraperipheral collisions. In recent years, the observation of coherent J/ ψ \psi photoproduction has been claimed in nucleus–nucleus (A–A) collisions with nuclear overlap, based on the measurement of an excess in the very low transverse momentum ( p T p_{\rm T} ) J/ ψ \psi yield.

arxiv-2410-17788.title: The Radio-Infrared Nebula in II Zw 40: Clusters Forming in Colliding Elongated Clouds 2024 The Radio-Infrared Nebula in II Zw 40: Clusters Forming in Colliding Elongated Clouds –
arxiv-2410-17788.creator: Dan Beilis Sara C. Beck, John Lacy, Jean L. Turner, Hauyu Baobab Liu, Paul T.P. Ho, S. Michelle Consiglio
arxiv-2410-17788.description: Abstract II Zw 40 is a starburst dwarf and merger product, and holds a radio-infrared supernebula excited by thousands of embedded OB stars. We present here observations of three aspects of the supernebula: maps of the K and KU radio continuum that trace dense ionized gas with spatial resolution ∼ 0.1 ′′ \sim 0.

arxiv-2503-07267.title: Phase field study of the effective fracture energy increase during dynamic crack propagation in disordered heterogeneous materials.
arxiv-2503-07267.creator: Hervé Henry
arxiv-2503-07267.description: Abstract The propagation of a 3D crack in an heterogeneous material is studied using a phase field model. It is shown that in the case of randomly distributed inclusions of soft material in a matrix, the nature of the distribution has little effect on the effective elastic properties. On the opposite it affects significantly crack propagation.

arxiv-2505-12982.title: Multi-parameter Control for the ( 1 + ( λ , λ ) ) (1+(\lambda,\lambda)) -GA on OneMax via Deep Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2505-12982.creator: Tai Nguyen, Phong Le, Carola Doerr, Nguyen Dang
arxiv-2505-12982.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tai Nguyen, Phong Le, Carola Doerr, Nguyen Dang. It is well known that evolutionary algorithms can benefit from dynamic choices of the key parameters that control their behavior, to adjust their search strategy to the different stages of the optimization process. A prominent example where dynamic parameter choices have shown a provable super-constant speed-up is the ( 1 + ( λ , λ ) ) (1+(\lambda,\lambda)) Genetic Algorithm optimizing the OneMax function.

arxiv-2506-04410.title: Matter-of-Fact: A Benchmark for Verifying the Feasibility of Literature-Supported Claims in Materials Science
arxiv-2506-04410.creator: Peter Jansen, Samiah Hassan, Ruoyao Wang
arxiv-2506-04410.description: Abstract Contemporary approaches to assisted scientific discovery use language models to automatically generate large numbers of potential hypothesis to test, while also automatically generating code-based experiments to test those hypotheses. While hypotheses can be comparatively inexpensive to generate, automated experiments can be costly, particularly when run at scale (i.e. thousands of experiments).

arxiv-2510-17059.title: Consistent Zero-Shot Imitation with Contrastive Goal Inference
arxiv-2510-17059.creator: Kathryn Wantlin, Chongyi Zheng, Ben Eysenbach
arxiv-2510-17059.description: Abstract In the same way that generative models today conduct most of their training in a self-supervised fashion, how can agentic models conduct their training in a self-supervised fashion, interactively exploring, learning, and preparing to quickly adapt to new tasks?

arxiv-2511-16619.title: Improving Long-Tailed Object Detection with Balanced Group Softmax and Metric Learning
arxiv-2511-16619.creator: Satyam Gaba
arxiv-2511-16619.description: Abstract Object detection has been widely explored for class-balanced datasets such as COCO. However, real-world scenarios introduce the challenge of long-tailed distributions, where numerous categories contain only a few instances. This inherent class imbalance biases detection models towards the more frequent classes, degrading performance on rare categories.

arxiv-2512-21009.title: ESCHER: Efficient and Scalable Hypergraph Evolution Representation with Application to Triad Counting * S. M. Shovan and Arindam Khanda contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2512-21009.creator: S. M. Shovan 3 * , Arindam Khanda 3 * , Sanjukta Bhowmick 2 , Sajal K. Das 3
arxiv-2512-21009.description: Abstract Higher-order interactions beyond pairwise relationships in large complex networks are often modeled as hypergraphs. Analyzing hypergraph properties such as triad counts is essential, as hypergraphs can reveal intricate group interaction patterns that conventional graphs fail to capture. In real-world scenarios, these networks are often large and dynamic, introducing significant computational challenges.

pmc-10741785.title: Cationic Porphyrins as Antimicrobial and Antiviral Agents in Photodynamic Therapy
pmc-10741785.creator: Inga O. Savelyeva, Kseniya A. Zhdanova, Margarita A. Gradova, Oleg V. Gradov, Natal’ya A. Bragina
pmc-10741785.description: Antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (APDT) has received a great deal of attention due to its unique ability to kill all currently known classes of microorganisms. To date, infectious diseases caused by bacteria and viruses are one of the main sources of high mortality, mass epidemics and global pandemics among humans.

pmc-11357633.title: Vorinostat Treatment of Gastric Cancer Cells Leads to ROS-Induced Cell Inhibition and a Complex Pattern of Molecular Alterations in Nrf2-Dependent Genes
pmc-11357633.creator: Leoni Lorenz, Tamara Zenz, Denys Oliinyk, Florian Meier-Rosar, Robert Jenke, Achim Aigner, Thomas Büch
pmc-11357633.description: Histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACi) show high antineoplastic potential in preclinical studies in various solid tumors, including gastric carcinoma; however, their use in clinical studies has not yet yielded convincing efficacies. Thus, further studies on cellular/molecular effects of HDACi are needed, for improving clinical efficacy and identifying suitable combination partners.

pmc-11415876.title: One in ten emergency medical calls in Slovenia originate from different location
pmc-11415876.creator: Špela Metličar, Larisa Žula, Nino Fijačko
pmc-11415876.description: cy of pinpointing the caller's location. The aim of this study is to investigate the callers' characteristics of 112 calls to the emergency medical services in Slovenia (Europe) and explore the challenges faced by Emergency Medical Dispatchers (EMDs). The study was carried out over a two-month period, between 15 June and 15 August 2024.

pmc-11458615.title: Mid- to long-term radiological and respiratory outcomes following surgery for older early-onset scoliosis patients with Marfan syndrome
pmc-11458615.creator: Yuki Taniguchi, Ryoji Tauchi, Teppei Suzuki, Haruhisa Yanagida, Kei Watanabe, Takachika Shimizu, Yoshitaka Matsubayashi, Noriaki Kawakami
pmc-11458615.description: This study aimed to elucidate mid- to long-term radiological and respiratory outcomes in patients aged 7–11 years at index surgery with Marfan syndrome and early-onset scoliosis (EOS) in a retrospective multicenter study. Primary outcomes were final thoracic height and final percentage of predicted vital capacity (%VC) at or after 16 years of age.

pmc-11510951.title: Efficient Degradation of Ofloxacin by Magnetic CuFe2O4 Coupled PMS System: Optimization, Degradation Pathways and Toxicity Evaluation
pmc-11510951.creator: Chuanhong Xing, Kang Chen, Limin Hu, Lanhua Liu
pmc-11510951.description: Magnetic CuFe2O4 was prepared with the modified sol–gel method and used for enhanced peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation and ofloxacin (OFL) degradation. The OFL could almost degrade within 30 min at a catalyst dosage of 0.66 g/L, PMS concentration of 0.38 mM, and initial pH of 6.53 without adjustment, using response surface methodology (RSM) with Box-Behnken design (BBD).

pmc-11533123.title: Copper-catalyzed yne-allylic substitutions: concept and recent developments
pmc-11533123.creator: Shuang Yang, Xinqiang Fang, Jaesook Yun
pmc-11533123.description: The catalytic (asymmetric) allylation and propargylation have been established as powerful strategies allowing access to enantioenriched α-chiral alkenes and alkynes. In this context, combining allylic and propargylic substitutions offers new opportunities to expand the scope of transition metal-catalyzed substitution reactions.

pmc-11578089.title: Functional genomics screens reveal a role for TBC1D24 and SV2B in antibody-dependent enhancement of dengue virus infection
pmc-11578089.creator: Laura Belmont, Maya Contreras, Catiana H. Cartwright-Acar, Caleb D. Marceau, Aditi Agrawal, Lisa M. Levoir, Jay Lubow, Leslie Goo
pmc-11578089.description: Under some conditions, dengue virus (DENV) can hijack IgG antibodies to facilitate its uptake into target cells expressing Fc gamma receptors (FcgR)—a process known as antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) of infection. Beyond a requirement for FcgR, host dependency factors for this unusual IgG-mediated infection route remain unknown.

pmc-11668342.title: Editorial: Applications of next generation sequencing (NGS) technologies to decipher the oral microbiome in systemic health and disease, volume II
pmc-11668342.creator: Thuy Do, Dongmei Deng, Naile Dame-Teixeira
pmc-11668342.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ntinues to explore the cutting-edge research on oral health and systemic diseases. Our first volume collated 17 insightful papers exploring the use of microbial meta-omics data to better understand the complex biological context of health and disease. These contributions provided a comprehensive overview of the current state of knowledge and future directions in the field of oral microbiome research using NGS technologies. NGS technologies hold immense potential for developing strategies to modulate the oral microbiome for improved overall health.

pmc-12984210.title: Multi-Modal Data Fusion for Quality Discrimination and Flavor Analysis of Commercial Oat Milk
pmc-12984210.creator: Leheng Jiang, Yuhao Cheng, Qiao Sun, Xiaoming Guo, Xiuping Dong, Yizhen Huang, Xiaojing Leng
pmc-12984210.description: In this study, 10 popular commercial oat milk samples were analyzed for sensory quality and flavor chemistry using the Ideal Profile Method (IPM), electronic nose (E-nose), and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Based on consumer cognitive mapping of ideal products, samples were classified into “Ideal-like” and “Ideal-exceeding” categories.

uslaw-usc-t42-s5891.title: 42 U.S.C. § 5891 — Sex discrimination prohibited
uslaw-usc-t42-s5891.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s5891.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 73 (Development Of Energy Sources); Subchapter IV (Sex Discrimination). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. No person shall on the ground of sex be excluded from participation in, be denied a license under, be denied the benefits of, or be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity carried on or receiving.
